text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.38% today to $151.37, capping a dramatic 10% surge over two weeks. The timing tells the story: the stock jumped $5.17 on October 23rd—the same day Brent crude hit a six-month high above $116 per barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions, including Trump's accusation that Iran was manipulating oil markets and reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Oil refiners and producers directly benefit when crude prices spike, since they sell oil at higher prices; the company also benefits from geopolitical risk premiums that push investors toward energy stocks during supply uncertainty.

The recent pullback in crude prices—down to $107.89 domestically and $115.22 globally—reflects renewed diplomatic efforts to ease the U.S.-Israeli-Iran conflict starting around October 26th. Yet ConocoPhillips held most of its gains rather than falling back with oil, suggesting investors may be pricing in a floor under energy prices if Middle East tensions remain elevated or diplomacy stalls.
